prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Create ONE standalone track-segment level-design concept image, part of a coherent six-image Bubbleport course design series, inspired by the modular running, obstacle and seated sliding sections of our teddy-bear slide game.
INPUT IMAGE: art-direction reference ONLY. Translate its physical miniature theme-park craftsmanship, ivory resin deck, mint and peach molded plastic, tiny brass connectors, warm inset lamps and translucent mint acrylic. DO NOT copy its entire layout, room, table, buildings, shops, ferris wheel or scenery.
CRITICAL CAMERA: TRUE TOP-DOWN ORTHOGRAPHIC PLAN VIEW, camera exactly vertically above, looking straight down. Image edges parallel to the track edges. Not isometric, not oblique, not a three-quarter render. Objects have realistic 3D material detail and short contact shadows, but only top faces and very small bevels are visible. A clean warm ivory studio background, not a wood table. One track segment only, not a collage, not a full level. Portrait composition for straight segments, generous but small margins, course fills image.
COMMON DESIGN: a wide continuous trough-like racecourse with ivory floor and low mint rails with peach corner caps, similar to our teddy-bear slide tracks. One common lane width of 19.2 design units, a reference character diameter of 1.3 units. Tiny warm signal lenses integrated in rails; no exterior buildings, plants, furniture or crowd. There is visible empty preparation space before every first obstacle and visible empty recovery space after the last. Both ends open for connection, never put an arch across the entry or exit. Simple painted arrowheads indicate travel from bottom to top. Preserve genuinely playable-looking connected floor and clearance; do not place decorations across the route. All motion information is diagrammatic, not additional solid obstacles.
GRAPHIC LANGUAGE: small clean title in top margin only, no paragraphs, no UI, no dimensions. Thin subtle dashed coral sweep envelopes and small bidirectional arrowheads may explain moving hazards, thin dashed teal line with arrowheads may explain ONE suggested player route. Keep these overlays sparse and readable, never obscure the floor. Soft near-photoreal miniature materials with controlled highlights and good contrast, crisp enough for a designer to study the exact obstacle positions.
No text except the specified title and optional small IN/OUT labels. No watermark. No teddy or marble characters. No extraneous obstacle types. Avoid giant blank margins and shallow-depth-of-field blur.
SPECIFIED TITLE: 06 星浪踏板
SEGMENT DESIGN:
STRAIGHT LEVEL APPROACH AND EXIT, width19.2 length64. Middle challenge is exactly FOUR transverse ROWS by THREE COLUMNS of large rounded rectangular ivory/mint FLOOR PANELS, 12 panels total, NOT raised tall cubes or solid barriers. Panel zonez16–48, with narrow seams and safe fixed transverse waiting ledges between rows. Panels sink slightly with a traveling-wave rhythm; depict selected panels darker mint with a visible shallow bevel edge, active safe panels cream; no deep black pits. Row1 center panel high; row2 left panel high; row3 center andright high; row4 right high; each row has at least one safe route. Unbroken fixed edge bypass strips on both sides each width2.6 provide a longer safe alternative, with low safety rails. Tiny signal lights near panel corners warn which tiles move; small vertical motion symbols kept on tile tops. Suggested teal route crosses safe panels in a readable left-center-right progression with small waits, not leaping across multiple rows. Bottom z0–10 clear, topz54–64 clear. Floor remains readable as a low platform puzzle suitable for running characters. No hammers, gates, can pillars or buildings.

corrections.prompt: Narrowly targeted edit of this existing Bubbleport track concept. Keep composition and all unmentioned elements unchanged. These floor tiles move UP AND DOWN IN HEIGHT, not laterally. REMOVE all coral dashed horizontal arcs and coral left-right double arrows above the rows. Keep the 12 tile-top small up/down symbols, all tile positions and colors, teal player route, pause symbols and the TWO fixed outer bypass strips. Also REMOVE the whole raised transverse end bar across bottom IN and top OUT so both deck ends are FULL-WIDTH OPEN, with the side rails simply terminating; keep IN and OUT as flat printed floor labels if necessary, no physical end wall. Preserve exact top-down camera, title, materials, floor and all other geometry. No new obstacles, no extra decorations, no redesign.
